chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: Stan Kenton's offer versus the Columbia staff job
summary: Lee agreed to join Stan Kenton but contractor Dave Klein urged him to take the Columbia staff job, which he did to stay with his son.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So he went in and he heard Johnny, and he just happened to stop in the Downbeat. He stopped in the Downbeat and he heard me, you know. I was his man. He was -- he wanted me and I was gonna join Stan's band; as a matter of fact, I've always been a 'word' man, and it was kind of embarrassing that I went back on my word. We negotiated the salary, you know, and we got up to like $350 -- and $350 then was a lot of money, you know? Because I didn't want to leave home ... because I didn't want to leave home because of my kid, you know, I had made some kind of vow or resolution to myself that I was gonna stay home until he was old enough to know.
But during the meantime when Stan really thought I was gonna join the band, and I had said I was gonna join the

band, but Dave Klein, who was the biggest contractor in town at the time, was Manny Klein's brother. He called me and said, 'How would you like to be on the staff at of Columbia Studios? They want you on the staff.' And I told him that I had this commitment with Stan, and I really wanted to go with the band, but I didn't want to leave home, but I wanted to play with the band, you know.

And, Davis was really one of the nicest men, and I think he did more for musicians than -- and helped musicians in more ways than he was probably ever given credit for. Now he talked to me like a father, you know. He explained to me how important this was for me to do this, you know; as a contractor, he said that he had tried to get black musicians on gigs and he had been turned down. And he knew that I could cut it, and I had to take the job because it would be others following me that I would set a good example because I was clean living and all, and I didn't drink or smoke, and you got to do it.

Now, that is not why I did it. You know. I'm just being honest about it. It was a good reason to do it, I guess, but if I had not made this vow about my son and had not been as close to him as I was, I would have gone with Stan Kenton, because you know how musicians are in spite of what Dave Klein was saying, because, you say, well, I'm not a politician, but that's really not about politics. That's probably what excuse
Iwould have used -- or had given myself.
